title: Governed Memory for Autonomous Agents A Critical Review of Provenance Temporal Validity and Access
content: Autonomous language-model agents need more than a searchable document collection. They must preserve observations, distinguish facts from inferences, update changing information, and construct a useful context under access and resource constraints. This review examines the database requirements created by those activities. It uses AI-native database as a functional design term for a data service supporting the agent memory lifecycle rather than as an established product category. A purposive narrative synthesis connects information retrieval, vector indexing, retrieval-augmented generation, agent memory, transaction isolation, and data provenance. The central contribution is a separation of authoritative records, append-only episodes, derived memories, and transient model context. A proposed record schema and retrieval workflow make provenance, temporal validity, authorization, and derivation explicit. The analysis explains why semantic similarity is insufficient for truth, why longer context does not replace memory management, and why deleting a source requires attention to derived summaries and embeddings. A hypothetical customer-support case illustrates conflict resolution and safe updates. A proposed mutation-sequence fixture links temporal validity, correction, derivative invalidation, and access enforcement to observable failures. No new database implementation or benchmark result is reported. The review argues that useful agent memory depends on controlled transformation and maintenance of evidence, not merely on retaining more tokens or selecting a particular storage engine.
